body:
## Context
The dashboard currently has several section-specific loading/error patterns:

- Model and history tables start with inline `Loading...` rows in `templates/index.html`.
- `makeTableEmptyState()` centralizes empty states only, not loading or error states.
- The chart reports errors through `#chart-note` and clears chart/legend manually.
- `loadOverview()`, `loadModels()`, `loadDaily()`, and `loadHistory()` have inconsistent catch behavior; some only `console.error()` without updating the visible UI.
- There is `.loading` / `.spinner` CSS, but it is not used as a shared state mechanism.

## Goal
Create a standardized, accessible loading/empty/error mechanism for dashboard sections so chart, model table, usage history, and summary cards behave consistently during fetches and failures.

## Suggested Scope
- Add small shared helpers for section state rendering, for example table loading/empty/error rows and chart loading/error notes.
- Ensure every async loader sets a visible loading state before fetch and a visible error state on failed requests or exceptions.
- Preserve source provenance and token-definition wording in all states.
- Keep hover/focus/tap accessibility intact.
- Add tests covering at least the template/helper wiring and visible error copy.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No inline duplicated `Loading...` table rows remain for model/history sections.
- `loadModels()`, `loadHistory()`, `loadDaily()`, and `loadOverview()` expose visible failure states, not only console logs.
- The chart has a clear loading state before data arrives and a clear empty/error state when source filters produce no data or fetches fail.
- Existing unit tests pass, and a UI smoke check confirms the rendered dashboard still loads.
title: Standardize dashboard loading, empty, and error states
